buckets.name: conventional
buckets.meaning: The claim's target is a conventional processor, whatever software steps the network.

buckets.name: simulated
buckets.meaning: The claim's target is a model of neuromorphic hardware that is not the silicon.

buckets.name: neuromorphic
buckets.meaning: The claim's target is fabricated neuromorphic silicon, or a custom spiking accelerator on an FPGA measured as its own target.

code.title: Input encoding and readout
code.text: Nearly all modern low-T conversion feeds the real-valued image as constant current, which makes layer one effectively an ANN layer. Readout cost and the decision window are rarely inside the reported measurement.

compute.title: Time model
compute.text: T means a different thing under a synchronous tick, an asynchronous event stream, and analog continuous time. Software timesteps do not map one to one onto hardware steps.

compute.title: Per-layer horizons
compute.text: No framework expresses a per-layer timestep horizon in one forward pass. TrueNorth, Loihi, Loihi 2 and Tianjic all advance through a single global barrier.

sw.title: Operator coverage
sw.text: lava_exchange dispatches only Linear, Conv2d, AvgPool2d and Flatten. Speck has no BatchNorm operator, so the DynapCNN mapper folds it into the preceding layer. Akida caps Dense input at 57,334 features and requires bounded ReLU.

sw.title: Reset semantics
sw.text: The sharpest seam. Conversion requires reset by subtraction, worth roughly twenty accuracy points. NIR does not distinguish it from reset to a value. SpikingJelly rejects it at both export paths. Loihi needs a two-compartment workaround that doubles neuron count.

left.title: Accuracy
left.text: What every reduction below trades against, and the reason the conversion literature exists.

left.title: Latency
left.text: Set by the time model, the horizon T, and how much spike traffic the fabric carries per inference.

left.title: Energy
left.text: Static and leakage power dominate measured energy on synchronous chips, so cutting T does not cut energy proportionally.

left.title: Availability
left.text: A chip you cannot obtain is a different answer from a chip that does not suit. Access gates and dormant toolchains belong on this axis.

right.title: Measurement
right.text: A SynOps figure is an operation-count ratio under an unstated hardware model, not joules. Boundary choices alone produce 14x swings for the identical chip and network.

right.title: Toolchain decay
right.text: SNN Toolbox last released March 2021. Intel archived all Lava repositories on 13 May 2026 with no maintenance and no patches accepted. The only toolchain that reached silicon is dormant.

right.title: Portability
right.text: NIR reaches nine simulators and five hardware platforms, turning m x n integrations into m + n. Its primitive set still does not distinguish the one semantics this literature depends on from reset to a value.

right.title: Two populations
right.text: The division of labor that no survey states. Algorithm papers advance accuracy at low T and do not deploy; none of the algorithm-population records reaches physical silicon, and Section 13.6, Population Counts, counts them. Every confirmed instance of a new method reaching silicon abandons rate coding.

snntoolbox-loihi1.name: SNN Toolbox to Loihi 1
snntoolbox-loihi1.story: A rate-coded converted MobileNet measured on physical Loihi 1 silicon at CIFAR-10 scale, reaching 8.52% error on 861 cores across 7 chips.
snntoolbox-loihi1.note: Historical. SNN Toolbox was last released on PyPI (0.6.0) in March 2021, its last GitHub release tag is v0.5.0 of June 2020, and its last code commit was in August 2022; the repository is not archived and took README-only commits in January 2023. Soft reset is an optional mode in the Intel bridge, not its default (reset_mode falls back to 'hard'), it doubles the compartments per neuron, and the paper does not state which mode the 8.52% run used, so the line draws the hard reset. NxTF is Keras-native and its host repository carries a discontinuation notice. Loihi 1 is superseded.

snntoolbox-spinnaker.name: SNN Toolbox to SpiNNaker 1
snntoolbox-spinnaker.story: A converted Keras LeNet on a physical 48-chip machine, 98.20% on MNIST at roughly 0.4 s wall-clock per sample with 15 ms of simulated activity.
snntoolbox-spinnaker.note: Nothing at CIFAR-10 scale or above was found on physical SpiNNaker silicon. The route runs the PyNN IF_curr_exp cell with a hard reset to zero and a 1000 ms membrane time constant, a current-based LIF that is effectively non-leaky over the 15 ms window. A timestep here is a timer interrupt, conventionally 1 ms, by default matched to real time.

sinabs-speck.name: Sinabs to Speck
sinabs-speck.story: The live conversion route that preserves reset by subtraction end to end, on hardware anyone can buy, measured at 3.36 us on Speck1 for a single event through nine 3x3 conv-and-pool layers at stride 1 and padding 1, pad to pad.
sinabs-speck.note: Sinabs from_model() defaults to MembraneSubtract(). Speck supports subtractive reset natively via return_to_zero=False. The IF label is the default; the optional leak is linear and driven by a slow clock. Speck has no BatchNorm operator, and DynapcnnNetwork folds BatchNorm into the preceding conv or linear layer automatically (merge_bn). A Demo Kit presold at $199, a price that comes from a June 2023 trade-press reprint of the SynSense release; no research-membership requirement is stated. Speck has no global clock, so T exists only at the raster-to-events boundary. The measured runs streamed external events and bypassed the on-die sensor, and the only classical-conversion run measured on Speck is N-MNIST at 86.17 percent; the gesture result on Speck was surrogate-gradient trained.

rockpool-xylo.name: Rockpool to Xylo
rockpool-xylo.story: Deployed quantized accuracy of 95.31 percent, with power measured on the HDK at 216 to 217 uW idle, 468 to 514 uW active and 251 to 298 uW dynamic, on audio and low-dimensional signals rather than vision.
rockpool-xylo.note: Xylo documents a synchronous time-stepped architecture with a global dt, so T here is a genuine hardware tick. Reset is by subtraction as a fixed hardware property. The measured run used a simulated audio encoder with events streamed from the host in accelerated time, so the microphone chip is documented, not exercised. The readout is the membrane potential in training and any-spike detection at test, and only the input encoder is rate-like, so no neural-code chip is drawn. Same vendor as Speck, opposite time model.

spikingjelly-lava.name: SpikingJelly to Lava to Loihi 2
spikingjelly-lava.story: The obvious modern route, and it does not complete.
spikingjelly-lava.note: The recipe drawn is SpikingJelly's rate-coding ReLU-to-IF conversion with max or percentile threshold calibration; the QCFS-based recipe's ActivationAwareIFNode is rejected by lava_exchange with NotImplementedError instead. Three independent blockers. The first is structural, since to_lava_blocks accepts a flat list, tuple or nn.Sequential while the recipe returns an FX GraphModule with VoltageScaler modules, so the converted network fails on shape before any neuron is inspected. Then lava_exchange raises ValueError("lava only supports for v_reset == 0!") at four call sites, plus an assertion in CubaLIFNode.__init__, rejecting the soft-reset neurons the rate-coding recipe produces by default. Then layer dispatch covers only Linear, Conv2d, AvgPool2d and Flatten, so a VGG MaxPool fails there; a ResNet skip connection fails for the structural reason, not in dispatch. Intel archived all Lava repositories on 13 May 2026.
spikingjelly-lava.breakWhy: The converted network fails on shape before any neuron is inspected, then its soft reset is rejected, then its layers are not dispatched. The conversion produced a network the framework’s own exporter will not accept.

spikingjelly-nxtf.name: SpikingJelly to NxTF to Loihi 1
spikingjelly-nxtf.story: Substituting the maintained framework into the route that actually reached silicon, and it does not connect.
spikingjelly-nxtf.note: The recipe drawn is SpikingJelly's rate-coding ReLU-to-IF conversion with max or percentile threshold calibration; the QCFS-based recipe's ActivationAwareIFNode is rejected by lava_exchange with NotImplementedError. NxTF inherits from the Keras Model and Layer interface. No bridge from a PyTorch SNN framework exists; SNN Toolbox ingests PyTorch ANNs through ONNX, and the only automated bridge into NxTF was specific to SNN Toolbox. The host repository carries a discontinuation notice, and INRC has redirected users to Lava since 2022. NxTF on Loihi 2 was not found.
spikingjelly-nxtf.breakWhy: NxTF is Keras-native and SpikingJelly is PyTorch. The framework boundary was only ever crossed automatically by an SNN-Toolbox-specific bridge that no longer has a maintained counterpart.

spikingjelly-nir.name: SpikingJelly to NIR
spikingjelly-nir.story: The portability route, blocked by an exporter that refuses to export what the specification does not distinguish.
spikingjelly-nir.note: The recipe drawn is SpikingJelly's rate-coding ReLU-to-IF conversion with max or percentile threshold calibration; the QCFS-based recipe's ActivationAwareIFNode is rejected by lava_exchange with NotImplementedError. NIR defines seventeen primitives, six of them neuron models (I, IF, LI, LIF, CubaLI, CubaLIF). All three spiking ones (IF, LIF, CubaLIF) document reset as v = v_reset when a spike fires, and no NIR field distinguishes reset by subtraction from reset to a value, so which one a backend applies is left to the backend. SpikingJelly nir_exchange raises NotImplementedError("NIR does not distinguish soft reset.") whenever v_reset is None, a deliberate and conservative refusal; other exporters (snnTorch, Sinabs) export the same neurons with v_reset = 0 and leave the discretization to the importer, so the block is SpikingJelly's exporter policy.
spikingjelly-nir.breakWhy: The broadest interchange format in the ecosystem does not distinguish reset by subtraction from reset to a value, and SpikingJelly’s exporter refuses rather than guess.

quantizeml-akida.name: QuantizeML to CNN2SNN to Akida
quantizeml-akida.story: A shipping commercial processor, where the conversion folds to a static threshold and the temporal dimension disappears.
quantizeml-akida.note: CNN2SNN computes y = x / act_step for Akida 1.0 layers, with a static threshold absorbing BatchNorm scale and shift, folded once at conversion time. No membrane potential carries across timesteps and no T is exposed. One paper (Ziegler et al.) describes it as squashing the rate-code approximation of ReLU into one time step, and a second (Lunghi et al.) says the converted model reduces the computation to a single time step. BrainChip states 4-bit or 8-bit quantized inputs to its layers, so the events are graded rather than binary, and no BrainChip source names a reset rule; the threshold is a static comparator applied in a single pass. The rank-order-coding heritage is genuine as input-stage heritage, but no source shows order sensitivity operating in converted hidden layers, so no neural-code chip is drawn.

quartz-loihi.name: Quartz to Loihi 1
quartz-loihi.story: A new method that reached silicon, by abandoning rate coding for TTFS.
quartz-loihi.note: Measured static, dynamic and total power, latency and energy per inference on a physical Nahuku 32 board, compared against the published NxTF numbers on the same platform (a different board, SDK version and network). The authors’ released implementation uses nxSDK 0.9.8 directly, as its code README states, while the paper's measurements were taken with NxSDK 1.0.0. The CIFAR-10 preferred energy-delay product uses an estimated static power, and the paper's 564 uJ energy label is a unit error for about 563 mJ.

slayer-loihi2.name: Lava-DL SLAYER to Loihi 2
slayer-loihi2.story: Direct training with a vendor toolchain, reaching silicon where rate-coded conversion did not.
slayer-loihi2.note: The workload drawn is the PilotNet sigma-delta network of Shrestha et al., Table 1, a steering regression from dashboard-camera frames measured on an Oheo Gulch single-chip Loihi 2 system with Lava-DL 0.4.0 and Lava 0.8.0; the int8 network ran at 0.09 mJ per inference without I/O, 1.21 ms latency and 7403.80 samples per second. A sigma-delta ReLU unit has no membrane or reset, so no neuron or reset chip is drawn, and steering regression has no task chip. The PilotNet LIF result is a vendor tutorial notebook, not a peer-reviewed measurement. Intel moved Loihi 2 toward graded sigma-delta payloads, citing Loihi 1 experience that rate-coded converted models suffer long latencies and inter-chip congestion. An ANN-to-sigma-delta conversion (Brehove et al.) was separately measured on a 16-chip Loihi 2 board. Intel archived the Lava repositories on 13 May 2026.

spikingjelly-gpu.name: SpikingJelly to a GPU
spikingjelly-gpu.story: The framework's own benchmark, timed end to end on an NVIDIA A100, where training a Spiking ResNet-18 with surrogate gradients reached up to 11x the speed of Norse (8x over snnTorch) at T = 32 and inference at ANN2SNN-scale T up to 2x.
spikingjelly-gpu.note: A conventional target. The paper states LIF neurons at SpikingJelly defaults with hard reset to zero, fed random 3x224x224 tensors at batch size 16 with mixed precision and no dataset. The training benchmark ran SpikingJelly's CuPy-compiled LIF kernels alongside PyTorch CUDA tensor operations, so nothing about a spiking substrate is measured. Training-iteration time was taken at T = 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32, and the ANN2SNN inference run is the same LIF network timed at T = 128 to 1024 with only T = 128 reported, on an Ubuntu 18.04 server with an Intel Xeon Silver 4210R host and 256 GB of memory.

mlgenn-gpu.name: mlGeNN to GeNN to a GPU
mlgenn-gpu.story: A converted VGG-16 and ResNet-20 simulated as GeNN-generated CUDA code on a 12 GB Titan V, with rate-based and few-spike conversion both evaluated on CIFAR-10 and only few-spike conversion run at ImageNet scale, on VGG-16 and ResNet-34.
mlgenn-gpu.note: A conventional target. On CIFAR-10 the converted VGG-16 ran 2.5x faster than BindsNET, the few-spike ResNet-20 a little over 2x slower than the original TensorFlow ANN at large batch sizes (at batch size 1 the same network is 3.5x faster than the ANN), and the fastest rate-based model over 100x slower than that ANN. Rate-based conversion used T = 2500 for VGG-16 and T = 1000 for ResNet-20; few-spike conversion used K = 10 and K = 8. The IF neurons use a hard reset to zero, stated in the paper and in ml_genn 1.0's if_neurons.py.

nest-cpu.name: PyNN and NEST to a CPU cluster
nest-cpu.story: A full-scale cortical microcircuit of about 80,000 LIF neurons and 0.3 billion synapses, simulated by NEST on a 32-node Intel Xeon cluster and compared head to head with SpiNNaker in the same paper.
nest-cpu.note: A conventional target. NEST runtime saturated around 3x real time with hybrid MPI and multithreading, and its lowest total energy came at about 144 threads and a 4.6x slowdown, where NEST and SpiNNaker had comparable energy per synaptic event. NEST used a 0.1 ms integration step. A separate performance report scales a later NEST-5g development build (a May 2017 snapshot) running the hpc_benchmark balanced random network from an SLI script under weak scaling to 82,944 nodes of the K computer, not the NEST 2.8 PyNN microcircuit run; there the connect phase stays near 80 seconds while prepare and run grow with node count. Not a classification workload; the record names no dataset, neural code or learning rule.

ttfs-cortex-m4.name: TTFS conversion to a Cortex-M4 MCU
ttfs-cortex-m4.story: A quantized 8-bit CNN converted with time-to-first-spike encoding among others and deployed on the ARM Cortex-M4 MCU, where Table 1 reports 48 microjoules and about 6 ms per inference at 87.9%, with the task unstated, against an analog Innatera chip in the same paper.
ttfs-cortex-m4.note: A conventional target. Energy, latency and accuracy were read with an external power analyzer under the MLPerf Tiny windowed protocol. The 8-bit CNN on the same MCU took 60 microjoules at 89.5%, and the same network on the Innatera SNP analog chip 24 microjoules and about 0.8 ms at 88.2%, so the energy reduction is 20 percent by the paper's own numbers, where the paper writes 23. The paper names TTFS among other encodings and also firing-rate control, and never states which encoding the measured digital SNN used. The pipeline is the paper's own, with layer-wise normalization and threshold calibration; CMSIS-NN is named only as a comparator framework, SNN Toolbox is not mentioned, and the part number is not named. The paper names CIFAR-10 and Google Speech Commands as example benchmarks and an 8-bit MobileNetV2 as its example architecture, but Table 1 is attributed to none of them, so no task chip is drawn. The source is weak in stated ways, a proposed evaluation framework whose Table 1 holds round values without the promised confidence intervals, gives latency as 6.00 ms and 6.1 ms in different sections, and states no neuron model or timestep count.

fenn-riscv.name: FeNN vector program to a RISC-V soft core
fenn-riscv.story: A recurrent spiking spoken-digit classifier stepped by a custom RISC-V vector instruction set on a soft core synthesized onto a Kria KV260 FPGA, reported significantly faster than a similar model on Loihi and twice as fast as an embedded GPU at half the energy.
fenn-riscv.note: A conventional target in this survey's vocabulary, a programmable RISC-V processor rather than a fixed-function spiking accelerator, even though it is realized on an FPGA. FeNN uses adaptive LIF neurons with subtractive reset and 16-bit fixed-point arithmetic with stochastic rounding. The SNN itself is RISC-V assembly emitted by a host-side C++ JIT assembler on the Kria's Cortex-A53; Vivado synthesizes the soft core once. The Loihi comparison is against the time Rao et al. report for a similar ALIF RSNN on Loihi, not a measurement in the FeNN paper, and the energy comparison is whole-board mains energy of the KV260 against a Jetson Orin Nano, both under desktop Linux. The SHD input is cochlea-model spike trains. FeNN-DMA, the follow-on system-on-chip, measured simulation throughput of a balanced random network of up to 16,000 neurons from on-chip performance counters and accuracy on Spiking Heidelberg Digits, N-MNIST and Braille; only its 0.53 W figure is a vectorless Vivado estimate rather than a board reading, while the 175 MHz clock and the LUT and FF counts are implementation results. The route is drawn under keyword spotting, the nearest task chip, while the record's task is spoken-digit classification.

adaptive-neuron.name: Adaptive / threshold-adaptive neuron (ALIF)
adaptive-neuron.summary: The firing threshold (or an equivalent subtractive after-hyperpolarizing current) increases after each spike and decays back toward baseline between spikes, implementing spike-frequency adaptation and LSTM-like long memory in recurrent SNNs. Native on BrainScaleS-2 (full AdEx analog circuit); on Loihi requires a 2-compartment AHP-current workaround.

akida.name: BrainChip Akida
akida.summary: Commercial neuromorphic NSoC family (AKD1000/AKD1500/Akida 2.0 IP/Akida Pico) whose converted-CNN deployment path (CNN2SNN/QuantizeML) collapses to a single feedforward pass over quantized, integer-only activations with a static per-neuron threshold that has absorbed folded BatchNorm scale/shift -- not a multi-timestep rate-coded IF/LIF accumulation. Lineage traces genuinely to Thorpe's rank-order-coding research (Spikenet Technology acquisition, 2016), but the order-sensitive shunting-inhibition mechanism has not been shown to operate inside converted-CNN hidden layers.

akida-runtime.name: Akida runtime
akida-runtime.summary: BrainChip's on-device execution stage: CNN2SNN's convert() output (a .fbz model) is loaded and run either on physical Akida hardware (AKD1000/AKD1500/Akida Pico silicon) or on BrainChip's own software simulator, with no membrane potential carried across timesteps and no user-exposed T; a nonzero (or newly-changed) quantized activation is the unit the runtime treats as an event.

akida-sim.name: Akida software backend
akida-sim.summary: BrainChip's own software simulator, on which the Akida runtime loads and runs the same CNN2SNN convert() output (a .fbz model) that it would send to AKD1000-class silicon. A run here claims software execution of the converted model's single feedforward pass on the host, not a measurement on Akida hardware; the Akida figures this survey cites as measured were taken on physical AKD1000-class hardware.

analog-time.name: Analog continuous time
analog-time.summary: Physical analog circuit dynamics evolve continuously rather than in discrete algorithmic steps; component values, not a digital clock, set how fast the circuit runs relative to biological real time.

ann2snn.name: SpikingJelly ann2snn
ann2snn.summary: SpikingJelly's ANN-to-SNN conversion module, rewritten (2026) into an FX-graph "recipe" framework: converter.py is now pure orchestration delegating to recipes/ (rate_coding.py, local_threshold_balancing.py, qcfs.py, etc.). The legacy Converter (branch 0.0.0.0.14, VoltageHook/VoltageScaler/IFNode) is the version most external tutorials describe; current master's flagship LocalThresholdBalancingRecipe implements a 2024/2025 CVPR paper (Bu, Li, Yu) rather than Rueckauer 2017, with a >50-point ImageNet/ResNet-18 accuracy gap between the two normalization granularities at matched T=32.

apex.name: APEX
apex.summary: RTL/cycle-level-simulated accelerator (Synopsys Design Compiler, 40 nm, 400 MHz) that integrates the PASC-IF neuron from the PASCAL conversion algorithm into the LoAS accelerator framework as a fully combinational circuit, targeting mixed INT4/INT8 precision and dual (spike + weight) sparsity. Not fabricated silicon.

async-events.name: Asynchronous event-driven
async-events.summary: No global clock: computation is triggered directly by the arrival of an individual event at each block, which independently computes its output as soon as its input is available, drawing no running power while idle. T exists only at the boundary where a discrete-time raster is converted into a stream of individually timestamped events; on-chip, there is no notion of a timestep at all.

backend-graph.name: Backend-specific graph
backend-graph.summary: The generic, non-portable internal model representation that sits between a training framework and a chip-specific compiler whenever no shared interchange format (such as NIR) is used. NxTF's Keras-derived DNN graph (Loihi), sPyNNaker's PyNN population/projection graph compiled by SpiNNTools into a per-core machine graph (SpiNNaker), the quantized Keras/ONNX graph QuantizeML hands to CNN2SNN's convert() (Akida), and Sinabs/Rockpool's mapper-specific network graphs (DynapCNN, Xylo) are all instances of this pattern: each is tied to its own framework and its own chip, and none is exchanged between vendors the way NIR is designed to be.

bidl.name: BIDL (Brain-Inspired Deep Learning)
bidl.summary: Lynxi's open-source PyTorch-based training/deployment framework (with the Nanhu Research Institute) for LIF/LIF+ neurons and hybrid ANN+SNN "DSNN" networks (Conv/BN/pooling ANN layers interleaved with ConvLIF/ConvLIAF SNN layers); compiles via the Lyngor compiler and executes via the LynSDK runtime on Lynxi chips.

binary-spikes.name: Binary spikes
binary-spikes.summary: The default single-bit address-event spike payload: a bare source/target/timestamp event with no magnitude information. The payload type essentially all classical, low-latency, and quantization-aware rate-coded conversion work assumes, and the default mode on every reviewed digital spiking platform.

biosignal-decoding.name: Biosignal decoding (EMG / EEG)
biosignal-decoding.summary: Gesture/movement decoding from surface EMG and seizure/motor-imagery decoding from scalp EEG both reach physical Loihi silicon with consistently large measured energy/latency advantages over GPU baselines; grouped separately from vision-based gesture recognition because the input modality is a sampled physiological time series.

brainscales-1.name: BrainScaleS-1
brainscales-1.summary: Heidelberg wafer-scale analog neuromorphic system (HICANN ASICs, 512 neurons/chip, ~10,000x accelerated analog time constants) that physically emulates AdEx/LIF neuron circuits rather than numerically simulating them; requires per-neuron calibration for manufacturing mismatch and hardware-in-the-loop training to reach usable accuracy for converted networks.

brainscales-2.name: BrainScaleS-2
brainscales-2.summary: Heidelberg single-chip analog neuromorphic ASIC (65 nm, 512 neurons x 512 synapses, two embedded digital plasticity processors) running ~1000x accelerated analog dynamics, with a non-spiking "hagen" MAC mode and a spiking LIF/AdEx mode; both require calibration plus hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) training because fixed-pattern mismatch and trial-to-trial analog noise prevent exact correspondence to a software IF/LIF model.

brian2.name: Brian2
brian2.summary: Neuroscience-first, differential-equation-defined neuron/synapse simulator with a Python front end and C++ code generation; GPU acceleration only via the separate Brian2GeNN bridge. Reaches deep converted CNNs only via SNN Toolbox as an external output backend, not through Brian2's own native API.

burst-coding.name: Burst coding
burst-coding.summary: A neuron may emit multiple spikes within or between a single simulation timestep when residual membrane potential after threshold crossing is large, rather than at most one spike per step; packs several rate-coding units of information into one step at the cost of within-step spike multiplicity.

cerebron.name: Cerebron
cerebron.summary: FPGA-based reconfigurable architecture (Xilinx XC7Z100, 200 MHz) explicitly built around the SNN Toolbox / Rueckauer-Diehl ANN-to-SNN conversion methodology, targeting spatiotemporal sparsity in standard, depthwise, and pointwise convolutions with an online channel-wise workload scheduler.

chemical-sensor-array.name: Chemical sensor array
chemical-sensor-array.summary: A wind-tunnel/chemosensor array whose readings are mapped onto a biologically derived olfactory-bulb-model spiking circuit; the sensing front end behind the survey's single most energy-efficient measured E1 Loihi result.

classical-conversion.name: Classical conversion
classical-conversion.summary: The founding threshold-balancing/weight-normalization ANN-to-SNN conversion methodology (Cao 2015, Diehl 2015, Rueckauer 2017, Sengupta 2019, and five further core algorithm papers). None of the nine core algorithm-proposing papers report any physical hardware execution; hardware validation of the methodology exists only in separate, later systems papers that adopt the conversion pipeline as an input rather than introducing it.

cnn2snn.name: BrainChip CNN2SNN / QuantizeML
cnn2snn.summary: BrainChip's official pipeline: QuantizeML performs uniform, symmetric, zero-centered integer quantization-aware training/PTQ; CNN2SNN convert() maps the quantized Keras/ONNX model to an Akida-runtime-compatible .fbz model, folding BatchNorm and activation-quantization math into per-neuron static thresholds (with a rounded half-step offset) so those operations "are never performed during inference" as separate floating-point ops.

codesigned-conversion.name: Hardware co-designed conversion
codesigned-conversion.summary: Conversion and post-training encoding methods that reach physical neuromorphic silicon by aligning the representation or neuron contract with platform execution. Located cases include Quartz TTFS on Loihi 1, Brehove sigma-delta graded payloads on Loihi 2, Adaptive Fission population coding on HP201, and complex Few-Spikes temporal coding on SpiNNaker2.

cortex-m-mcu.name: ARM Cortex-M MCU
cortex-m-mcu.summary: An ARM Cortex-M-family microcontroller executing a converted SNN as compiled embedded firmware. The survey's evidence records measure a CNN-to-SNN, time-to-first-spike-converted digital SNN on a Cortex-M4 MCU (exact part not named in the retrieved text), read with an external power analyzer under the MLPerf Tiny windowed-measurement protocol.

cpu-generic.name: Conventional CPU
cpu-generic.summary: A general-purpose CPU, single or clustered, running an SNN as a program of NEST's own C++ simulation kernel rather than any dedicated spiking substrate. The survey's evidence records measure NEST on a 32-node Intel Xeon E5-2680v3 HPC cluster (comparator SpiNNaker measured in the same paper) and NEST-5g on up to 82,944 Fujitsu SPARC64 VIIIfx compute nodes of the K computer.

cuba-lif.name: Current-based LIF (CUBA-LIF)
cuba-lif.summary: Separates a first-order synaptic-current state u (its own decay tau_u) from the membrane-voltage state v: u(t) = alpha_u*u(t-1) + weighted-spike-input; v(t) = alpha_v*v(t-1) + u(t) + bias. Loihi's native baseline neuron model and the default neuron type in Lava-DL's SLAYER cuba block and NetX HDF5 schema.

direct-input-encoding.name: Direct / analog / constant-current input encoding
direct-input-encoding.summary: Real-valued input (e.g. pixel intensities) is applied as a constant analog input current to the first hidden layer at every timestep instead of first converting it to spikes; the first layer then performs a genuine (potentially multi-bit) MAC, forfeiting the accumulate-only efficiency the rest of the SNN enjoys, in exchange for materially improving conversion accuracy (Rueckauer 2017: CIFAR-10 ~59.8% Poisson vs. 83.6% direct current, same normalization).

direct-training-surrogate-gradient.name: Direct training by surrogate gradient / BPTT
direct-training-surrogate-gradient.summary: Train an SNN end-to-end via backpropagation-through-time with a surrogate (smooth) derivative substituted for the non-differentiable spike function. The dominant paradigm behind SpikingJelly's SEW-ResNet/Spikformer/Spike-driven-Transformer image-classification lineage and STBP-derived robotics-control policies.

dynap-se2.name: DYNAP-SE2
dynap-se2.summary: SynSense/INI Zurich mixed-signal analog neuromorphic ASIC (1024 analog AdExpIF neurons in 2x2 16x16-neuron cores, 4-bit configurable synaptic weight); its own companion simulator DynapSim explicitly does not numerically match the hardware, and no rate-coded ANN-to-SNN conversion pipeline for this chip was located in the sources reviewed.

dynapcnn.name: SynSense DYNAP-CNN
dynapcnn.summary: Standalone predecessor processor core to Speck (12 mm^2, 22 nm, over 1M Integrate-and-Fire neurons, 4M programmable parameters), scalable via daisy-chained devices; the same asynchronous, clockless, sub-5 ms latency architecture minus the integrated DVS sensor.

dynapcnn-mapper.name: DynapcnnNetwork (Sinabs mapper)
dynapcnn-mapper.summary: Sinabs's DynapcnnNetwork(discretize=True) restructures a sequential Sinabs SNN into DynapcnnLayer objects (conv->spike->pool), discretizes weights to 8-bit and membrane/thresholds to 16-bit, auto-converts nn.Linear to 1x1 Conv2d and nn.AvgPool2d to SumPool2d, and places layers onto physical cores via chip_layers_ordering="auto" (raises an error if no valid placement fits per-core memory).

event-camera.name: Event camera (DVS)
event-camera.summary: A commercial dynamic-vision-sensor (DVS) chip outputting an asynchronous stream of (x, y, timestamp, polarity) address-event tuples over USB3 or MIPI CSI-2, plus, on some models, a secondary low-bandwidth raw AER pin header intended for direct neuromorphic-hardware interfacing. Event-based/neuromorphic in its sensing principle, but its primary production interface is the same USB3/MIPI path used by conventional CMOS image sensors.

fenn-vector-program.name: FeNN Vector-ISA SNN Program
fenn-vector-program.summary: FeNN's custom RISC-V vector instruction set extension (a CV32E40X scalar core plus a custom vector co-processor), whose program, RISC-V assembly emitted by a host-side C++ JIT assembler, steps adaptive LIF (ALIF) neuron and synapse state updates across timesteps; FeNN-DMA extends the same instruction set with DMA-based synaptic-weight streaming for larger networks.

fenn-vivado-toolchain.name: FeNN Vivado RTL Synthesis Toolchain
fenn-vivado-toolchain.summary: AMD/Xilinx Vivado 2023.2, which synthesizes FeNN's custom RISC-V vector-processor RTL design (SystemVerilog) into a bitstream realized as a soft core on a Kria KV260 FPGA board. FeNN-DMA's own post-implementation figures from the same toolchain report 175 MHz (single-core) and 143 MHz (dual-core) operating frequency, 0.53 W dynamic power, and 54,984 LUTs / 47,759 FFs of resource usage.

fpga.name: FPGA SNN accelerators (general)
fpga.summary: General-purpose FPGA family used across the survey for custom SNN accelerator implementations (SyncNN, Spiker/Spiker+, FireFly/v2, Cerebron, and others). Faithfulness to IF+reset-by-subtraction+rate-coding varies per design; several (Spiker+, SyncNN) offer reset-by-subtraction as an explicit, user-selectable configuration, while others (FireFly) do not document reset polarity at all.

fpga-truenorth-emulation.name: TrueNorth FPGA emulation
fpga-truenorth-emulation.summary: An FPGA-based emulation environment for neuromorphic architectures that reimplements IBM TrueNorth's five per-core components (neuron block, core SRAM, router, scheduler, token controller) as a reference design realized on a Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC ZCU102 development board (XCZU9EG FPGA), validated against IBM's own Compass simulator on MNIST and vector-matrix-multiplication case studies. An FPGA emulating a named chip; a run here claims the emulated design's behavior, not a measurement on TrueNorth silicon.

frame-camera.name: Frame camera
frame-camera.summary: A conventional CMOS/global-shutter image sensor producing dense RGB or grayscale frames at a fixed frame rate, delivered over USB3 or MIPI CSI-2. Not event-based; the source of the static-frames representation for classical/low-latency/quantization-aware ANN-to-SNN conversion and for any converted-CNN deployment, and, for benchmark datasets such as MNIST/CIFAR/ImageNet, often not a physical sensor at all but a pre-captured, distributed dataset.

frames-from-events.name: Frames reconstructed from events
frames-from-events.summary: A dense frame or voxel-grid tensor built by accumulating an asynchronous event stream over a fixed time window, then handed to a conventional (non-spiking) CNN or Transformer. Documented as the dominant, default practice in the event-vision deep-learning literature, not a minority special case, and no spiking route in this survey passes through it: every downstream deployment observed from this representation targets GPU, embedded CPU/Jetson, or a conventional FPGA CNN accelerator (Vitis-AI DPU), never a spiking chip.

genn-cuda.name: GeNN CUDA Code Generation
genn-cuda.summary: GeNN's code-generation backend, to which mlGeNN's converted-CNN model description compiles down as generated CUDA C++ simulation code. mlGeNN's own benchmark reports its converted VGG-16 CIFAR-10 inference as 2.5x faster than BindsNET and its FewSpike ResNet-20 conversion as only a little over 2x slower than the original TensorFlow ANN, both on an NVIDIA Titan V GPU.

gesture-recognition.name: Gesture recognition
gesture-recognition.summary: The single most consistently demonstrated genuinely end-to-end (sensor-to-spiking-chip) neuromorphic application in the survey, spanning DVS-based and EMG-based variants across nearly every major spiking platform, and the one task category where direct BPTT training, spike-time-gradient training, and rate-coded conversion have all independently reached physical silicon.

gpu-generic.name: Conventional GPU
gpu-generic.summary: A general-purpose graphics processor running an SNN as a program of ordinary PyTorch or GeNN-generated CUDA kernels rather than any dedicated spiking substrate. The survey's evidence records measure an NVIDIA A100-SXM-80GB GPU (SpikingJelly's own PyTorch-CUDA training and ANN2SNN inference benchmark) and an NVIDIA Titan V GPU (mlGeNN's GeNN-generated CUDA simulation of a converted VGG-16 and ResNet-20).

graded-spikes.name: Graded spikes
graded-spikes.summary: A spike event whose payload carries a multi-bit (typically signed integer) magnitude rather than a bare 0/1, letting one event transmit a quantized activation delta directly instead of a count of binary spikes accumulated over T timesteps. Native to Loihi 2 via signed integer payloads (up to 24 bits per Shrestha et al. 2023, a 32-bit field per Intel's Loihi 2 brief, up to 16 bits per Brehove et al.) and dedicated sigma-delta microcode; the hardware feature underlying graded/sigma-delta ANN-to-SNN conversion.

hand-designed-hybrid-finetuning.name: Hand-designed and hybrid fine-tuning
hand-designed-hybrid-finetuning.summary: Pipelines that combine a hand-designed or conventionally trained component with a lightweight, hardware-specific correction step, short of full hardware-in-the-loop backpropagation -- e.g. a chip-specific weight-rescaling/quantization step layered on top of gradient training, or direct-training results benchmarked head-to-head against conversion on the same chip.

hardware-in-the-loop-training.name: Hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) training
hardware-in-the-loop-training.summary: Forward pass executed on physical analog silicon; backward pass / gradient computed in software using an approximate (e.g. ReLU-derivative) model of the intractable hardware activation function, injecting hardware-measured quantities into the computation graph. The practical countermeasure BrainScaleS deployments use in place of relying on exact IF/LIF correspondence, which fixed-pattern mismatch and trial-to-trial analog noise make unattainable.

host-io.name: Host encoding and readout
host-io.summary: The host-side (non-spiking-core) encoding and readout step every reviewed digital platform still depends on: converting an input into the chip's native event/packet format before injection, and converting output spikes/counters back into a readable result after execution finishes.

hxtorch.name: hxtorch
hxtorch.summary: PyTorch interface to BrainScaleS-2 with two operating modes: non-spiking "hagen" mode (matmul/conv primitives executed directly on hardware as analog vector-matrix multiplication) and hxtorch.snn (LIF/LI spiking layers with hardware-in-the-loop training, CADC-sampled membrane traces injected into the PyTorch autograd graph).

hxtorch-sim.name: hxtorch mock simulation
hxtorch-sim.summary: hxtorch's mock mode, enabled by setting mock=True in the Experiment instance, which runs the same hxtorch.snn LIF and LI layers as a numerical simulation on the host instead of on the BrainScaleS-2 chip. BrainScaleS-2's own documentation distinguishes this from genuine hardware execution, whose returned hardware data are mapped to a dense time grid. A run here claims a simulation, not a BrainScaleS-2 measurement.

hybrid-finetuning.name: Hybrid SNN-ANN fine-tuning
hybrid-finetuning.summary: A pipeline that trains part of a network as a conventional ANN and part as an SNN (rather than a single end-to-end spiking network or a pure conversion), then deploys the hybrid model to physical hardware via a vendor toolchain bridge. Distinct from hand-designed-hybrid-finetuning's chip-specific calibration/rescaling step: here the hybridization is architectural (ANN layers plus SNN layers in one model), not a post-hoc correction on top of an otherwise pure SNN.

if-neuron.name: Integrate-and-fire (IF) neuron, nonleaky
if-neuron.summary: V(t) = V(t-1) + z(t), spike when V(t) >= threshold, no decay term; the canonical neuron of the ANN-to-SNN conversion literature because, under reset-by-subtraction and constant/rate input, its time-averaged firing rate is an unbiased estimator of the ReLU activation it was converted from.

image-classification-static.name: Image classification (static frames)
image-classification-static.summary: MNIST/CIFAR/ImageNet-scale classification of static images; historically the primary evaluation target of both classical and low-latency (QCFS-lineage) ANN-to-SNN conversion, and the task this thesis's own QCFS/QCFS+/QCFS++ tracks build on.

imu-analog-sensor.name: IMU and analog sensors
imu-analog-sensor.summary: Proprioceptive and analog physical sensing that is neither a camera nor a microphone: IMU/inertial data, joint encoder feedback, force-torque sensors, and surface-EMG electrodes. Feeds the time-series representation for robotics/control and biosignal-decoding workloads rather than a vision or audio pipeline.

innatera-pulsar.name: Innatera Pulsar
innatera-pulsar.summary: Commercial mixed-signal neuromorphic microcontroller (TSMC 28 nm, 2Q25 production) integrating both an analog SNN engine and a separate digital SNN engine alongside an INT8 CNN accelerator and a RISC-V core; marketed as ultra-low-power always-on edge sensing. All quantitative performance claims located in this research are vendor-sourced, with no independent third-party peer-reviewed benchmark found.

keyword-spotting-audio.name: Keyword spotting and audio classification
keyword-spotting-audio.summary: The strongest commercial, purpose-built, directly-trained-SNN deployment pipeline found in the survey (SynSense Xylo), which beats both Loihi and SpiNNaker2 on the same benchmark task in a head-to-head published comparison table.

lava.name: Lava (core)
lava.summary: Intel's open-source, platform-agnostic Process/Process-model framework (CSP-style) with a low-level Magma compiler/runtime layer; the specific Magma components compiling to Loihi hardware are proprietary and gated to INRC members. Archived by Intel as of ~2026-05-13 ("stay tuned for announcements about our new SDK").

lava-dl.name: Lava-DL
lava-dl.summary: Intel's deep-learning library within Lava (lava.lib.dl): slayer (SLAYER 2.0 direct training), bootstrap (fast rate-coded-SNN training via ANN surrogate), and netx (HDF5-to-Lava-Process inference deployment). Archived alongside core Lava.

lava-exchange.name: SpikingJelly lava_exchange
lava-exchange.summary: SpikingJelly module implementing the documented pipeline SpikingJelly -> Lava DL -> Lava -> Loihi: data-layout conversion ([T,N,*] to [N,*,T]), IF/LIF-to-CubaLIFNode conversion via BlockContainer, export_hdf5() producing the same HDF5 schema lava.lib.dl.netx consumes.

lava-loihi-sim.name: Lava Loihi simulator
lava-loihi-sim.summary: Lava's CPU-side simulation backend, on which a Process's software model runs the same LIF neurons and Lava processes that the Loihi backend would run, so that a network can be prototyped on conventional CPUs and GPUs before any chip is involved. A run here claims a software emulation of Loihi's behavior, not execution on Loihi silicon.

lava-runtime.name: Lava ProcessModels
lava-runtime.summary: The Magma-layer execution runtime within Lava that actually runs a compiled ProcessModel on physical Loihi 2 hardware (the Loihi2HwCfg backend), reached from NetX-compiled network descriptions produced by SLAYER/Bootstrap training or by SpikingJelly's lava_exchange export when it succeeds. The Loihi-targeting Magma components are proprietary and gated to INRC members; the same ProcessModel abstraction can alternatively execute in a CPU/software simulation backend with no hardware involved. Archived by Intel as of 2026-05-13 with no further maintenance or patches accepted.

lif-neuron.name: Leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron
lif-neuron.summary: Adds an exponential leak term to the IF membrane update: V(t) = alpha*V(t-1) + z(t), alpha = exp(-dt/tau) < 1. Standard default on SpiNNaker (IF_curr_exp), Xylo, Spiker, and as a general Lava-DL/NIR primitive.

local-learning-plasticity.name: Local learning and plasticity rules
local-learning-plasticity.summary: Hand-designed, biologically derived spiking circuits with local (often STDP-family or one-shot) on-chip plasticity rather than global backpropagation. This is where the largest and most rigorously measured E1 evidence base on Loihi actually concentrates (olfaction, SLAM, sparse coding/LASSO, SAT/CSP), not the surrogate-gradient/BPTT lineage that dominates the SpikingJelly ecosystem.

loihi-1.name: Intel Loihi 1
loihi-1.summary: First-generation Intel neuromorphic research chip (14 nm, 128 cores, up to 131,072 neurons); native CUBA-LIF neuron with hard reset-to-zero, requiring a two-compartment trick for reset-by-subtraction. Superseded by Loihi 2 and now accessible only through the discontinued NxSDK/NxTF software path.

loihi-2.name: Intel Loihi 2
loihi-2.summary: Second-generation Intel neuromorphic chip (Intel 4 process, up to 1M neurons/chip) with a fully microcode-programmable neuron engine and native graded (up to 32-bit signed payload) spikes, enabling sigma-delta and Resonate-and-Fire neurons beyond CUBA-LIF. Its software stack (Lava/Lava-DL/NetX) was archived by Intel around 2026-05-13 with no announced successor.

low-latency-conversion.name: Low-latency conversion
low-latency-conversion.summary: Recent low-timestep ANN-to-SNN conversion methods based on spike counts or firing rates. In the audited corpus, none of the proposing papers measures its own new rate-coded method on named physical neuromorphic silicon.

lynxi-ka200.name: Lynxi KA200
lynxi-ka200.summary: Commercial compute-in-memory, many-core heterogeneous-fusion chip from Lynxi (spinout building on the Tianjic lineage), natively supporting both deep-learning ANNs and brain-inspired SNNs with mixed-precision compute; deployment path (BIDL/Lyngor/LynSDK) is effectively unavailable outside mainland China per sources reviewed.

microphone.name: Microphone
microphone.summary: A conventional audio sensor delivering a sampled PCM waveform, the input modality behind most keyword-spotting and speech benchmarks in the survey; not event-based, but the resulting sampled time series is what a directly trained SNN (Xylo, Loihi) or Akida's converted keyword spotter consumes.

mlgenn.name: mlGeNN
mlgenn.summary: GPU code-generation-based conversion library adding explicit deep-CNN support atop GeNN; demonstrated VGG-16 and ResNet-34/20 converted and evaluated at real CIFAR-10 and ImageNet scale (VGG-16: 70.2% vs. 70.3% ANN baseline on ImageNet). The ImageNet result is E1 on a GPU, a measured run on a conventional target, and E5 for any neuromorphic claim; no route to a neuromorphic ASIC target is documented.

morphic.name: MorphIC
morphic.summary: UCLouvain academic quad-core, binary-weight digital neuromorphic ASIC (65 nm, 738k synapses/mm^2, stochastic spike-driven online learning) that provides the clearest controlled, same-silicon comparison of rate coding versus rank-order coding energy cost on the identical MNIST task.

multi-compartment.name: Multi-compartment
multi-compartment.summary: A neuron model split into two or more linked compartments holding separate state variables, used on digital chips as a workaround to implement mechanisms the native single-compartment neuron cannot express directly. On Loihi, the load-bearing use is reset-by-subtraction: because Loihi's native hard reset only zeroes the membrane, a second compartment configured to inhibit the first by exactly the threshold amount is needed to reproduce soft reset, doubling the compartment cost of every neuron that needs it.

native-events.name: Native event stream
native-events.summary: The raw, unreconstructed asynchronous (x, y, t, polarity) address-event stream from an event camera or other neuromorphic sensor, consumed directly by an event-driven spiking chip with no intervening frame buffer.

nengo.name: Nengo
nengo.summary: Implements the Neural Engineering Framework (NEF): analytically-solved decoding weights over spiking-neuron tuning curves, a fundamentally different construction from backprop-trained rate matching. NengoDL bridges to Keras/TensorFlow-style training and provides a Converter that swaps ReLU for spiking equivalents (rate-coded ANN-to-SNN conversion as one of its modes).

nengo-loihi.name: NengoLoihi
nengo-loihi.summary: Backend compiling a Nengo network (built via NEF or via NengoDL ReLU-to-spiking conversion) onto Loihi; models discretized neuron activation profiles (LoihiLIF/LoihiSpikingRectifiedLinear classes) during training, respects the 1024-neurons/core limit, and ships both a Loihi emulator and a physical-hardware backend using Intel's proprietary NxSDK on a "superhost" wired to physical boards.

nest.name: NEST
nest.summary: Purpose-built for parallelized simulation of large, densely-connected recurrent networks of point neurons (biologically-realistic cortical-microcircuit scale); exposed as a PyNN backend for ANN2SNN pipelines built on top of it (e.g. via SNN Toolbox), but has no native CNN-conversion capability of its own.

nest-kernel.name: NEST Simulation Kernel
nest-kernel.summary: NEST's own C++ simulation kernel, which executes a PyNN-described point-neuron network directly as a software program. The survey's evidence records measure the kernel's MPI+multithreaded runtime and per-synaptic-event energy against physical SpiNNaker hardware on an Intel Xeon HPC cluster, and its weak-scaling connect, prepare, and run wall-clock time up to 82,944 K-computer SPARC64 nodes.

netx.name: Lava-DL NetX
netx.summary: lava.lib.dl.netx.hdf5.Network(net_config=...) reconstructs a platform-independent HDF5 network description (produced by SLAYER/Bootstrap training or by SpikingJelly's lava_exchange export) as a runnable Lava Process graph, executable on CPU simulation or, for INRC members, physical Loihi 2 hardware by switching the RunConfig (e.g. Loihi2HwCfg vs. a CPU sim config).

neuroflex.name: NeuroFlex
neuroflex.summary: RTL/cycle-level-simulated accelerator (Synopsys Design Compiler, 40 nm, 560 MHz) extending PASCAL's layer-level lossless ANN/SNN equivalence to column-level hybrid execution, where individual output columns within one layer independently run in ANN mode or PASC-IF SNN mode chosen by a profiling-driven scheduler. Not fabricated silicon.

nir.name: Neuromorphic Intermediate Representation (NIR)
nir.summary: A unified graph IR (Nature Communications 2024) whose documentation defines seventeen primitives (the paper lists eleven computational and three higher-order primitives), read/written by 9 simulators and reaching 5 hardware platforms (BrainScaleS-2, Loihi 2, Speck, SpiNNaker2, Xylo). Verified directly against the reference implementation's neuron primitive source (nir/ir/neuron.py): six of the seventeen are neuron models (CubaLI, CubaLIF, I, IF, LI, LIF); all three spiking primitives (IF, LIF, CubaLIF) specify reset identically as reset-to-a-fixed-value (v <- v_reset if spike else v, v_reset defaulting to 0). No NIR field distinguishes reset by subtraction from reset to a value; which one a backend applies is left to the backend, so an exporter that refuses subtractive-reset neurons does so by its own policy. Hardware backends are explicitly permitted to simply ignore unsupported nodes rather than approximate them.

nir-exchange.name: SpikingJelly nir_exchange
nir-exchange.summary: SpikingJelly's specific NIR import/export module; to_nir.py's _hard_reset() function raises NotImplementedError unconditionally whenever a neuron's v_reset is None (SpikingJelly's soft-reset convention), i.e. this specific exporter implementation never implements the subtractive-reset branch even though the exported IR format's own maintainers (NIR spec) do define one.

no-physical-sensor.name: No sensor (dataset or solver)
no-physical-sensor.summary: Workloads with no physical transducer at all: a problem instance (a sparse-coding dictionary, a CNF/DPLL-style Boolean formula) is encoded directly into spiking-network structure and dynamics, or a benchmark dataset is loaded from disk rather than sensed live.

norse.name: Norse
norse.summary: PyTorch-based SNN library whose documented LIFCell/LIFRecurrentCell default to reset-to-zero (v_reset defaults to 0, hard-reset equation v=(1-z)v+z*v_reset); exports to NIR (norse.to_nir), with a documented caveat that round-trip export/import produces different spike patterns on identical input.

northpole.name: IBM NorthPole
northpole.summary: IBM's 2023 successor architecture (12 nm, 22B transistors, 256 cores, 192 MB distributed SRAM) explicitly described by IBM as an extension of TrueNorth, but purely digital, low-precision (8/4/2-bit) MAC-based inference NPU with no spiking/event-driven neuron model or membrane potential dynamics -- efficiency gains derive from memory-locality and low-bit MAC execution, not event-driven temporal sparsity.

nxsdk.name: NxSDK
nxsdk.summary: Intel's Loihi 1 software development kit and register-level NxCore driver API; supported three high-level front ends (third-party Nengo, Intel's own NxNet, and NxTF) all compiling down through NxCore. Loihi-1-era; superseded by Lava for Loihi 2 per INRC's own 2022 migration guidance, which directs members to Lava for Loihi 2.

nxtf.name: NxTF
nxtf.summary: Intel's Keras-Model/Layer-derived DNN compiler within NxSDK for Loihi 1, distinct from the low-level NxNet API; trades NxNet's generality for CNN-focused compilation exploiting weight-sharing to compress models across cores. Explicitly built an interface between NxTF and SNN Toolbox (nxsdk_modules_ncl/dnn/.../snntoolbox). Superseded; INRC has directed users to Lava since 2022; intel-nrc-ecosystem/models carries a blanket "DISCONTINUATION OF PROJECT" notice.

object-detection.name: Object detection
object-detection.summary: Automotive and drone/robotics object detection built on event cameras or RGB video, overwhelmingly executed on conventional CNN accelerators (FPGA Vitis-AI DPU, GPU). No peer-reviewed report found of an object detector measured on physical rate-coded/IF spiking silicon; the one E1 spiking exception uses a non-rate-coded graded-spike (sigma-delta) conversion scheme on Loihi 2.

olfaction.name: Olfaction (odor classification)
olfaction.summary: The single most energy-efficient measured E1 Loihi result in the survey (single-shot learning, sub-millijoule per classification), but built on a hand-designed, locally-plastic biological circuit rather than gradient training; its algorithmic generalization claim is independently contested.

optimization-constraint-satisfaction.name: Optimization and constraint satisfaction
optimization-constraint-satisfaction.summary: Alongside olfaction, this is where the deepest and most consistently measured body of E1 Loihi evidence in the entire survey lives. Every instance found is a hand-designed spiking algorithm (Locally Competitive Algorithm for sparse coding/LASSO, SAT/CSP solving), never a gradient-trained network and never an ANN-to-SNN conversion.

pasc-if.name: PASC-IF (spike-accumulation IF neuron)
pasc-if.summary: PASCAL's IF variant using spike accumulation and adaptive layerwise activation with soft reset and explicit inhibitory (negative) spikes; proven exactly equivalent to a QCFS-activation ANN with required timesteps T=L per layer (vs. QCFS's typical ~1024), rather than the classical hard/subtractive reset conventions used elsewhere in this survey.

phase-coding.name: Phase coding / weighted spikes
phase-coding.summary: Spikes are assigned a weight depending on which phase (position within a repeating K-timestep cycle) they occur in, typically powers of two (2^(K-1),...,2^0), producing a non-uniform (binary, exponentially-weighted) effective quantization grid -- the spike-domain analogue of non-uniform (e.g. logarithmic) quantization, in contrast to rate coding's uniform grid.

population-coding.name: Population coding
population-coding.summary: A value is represented jointly by the activity pattern across a population of neurons (tuning curves, ensemble firing-rate vectors, or which neurons fire) rather than by one neuron's rate or timing; an orthogonal (spatial-multiplexing) axis that can co-occur with rate or temporal codes rather than a fourth encoding primitive.

pynn.name: PyNN
pynn.summary: Simulator-independent Python API for building neuronal network models, runnable unmodified across NEURON, NEST, Brian, and, critically, two physical neuromorphic hardware backends: SpiNNaker (pyNN.spiNNaker via sPyNNaker) and BrainScaleS (pynn_brainscales.brainscales2). Does not itself define neuron reset semantics or time model -- inherited from whichever backend executes the model.

pytorch-cuda.name: PyTorch CUDA Backend
pytorch-cuda.summary: PyTorch's CUDA execution backend, which SpikingJelly's neuron, synapse, and encoding modules dispatch to as ordinary tensor operations. SpikingJelly's own documentation describes a CUDA-accelerated execution path for its neuron modules, and its Science Advances benchmark reports up to 11x training speedup and up to 2x ANN2SNN inference speedup on an NVIDIA A100 GPU relative to Norse and snnTorch.

quant-aware-conversion.name: Quantization-aware conversion
quant-aware-conversion.summary: Conversion methods that bind quantization choices to timesteps or thresholds. QAC and MT-SNN implement static layerwise horizons with explicit temporal alignment. Their reported mean timestep values are software summaries, not hardware latency.

quantizeml.name: QuantizeML
quantizeml.summary: BrainChip's quantization-aware-training / post-training-quantization front end for the Akida toolchain: converts a float Keras/ONNX CNN into an integer-only model using uniform, symmetric, zero-centered quantization with a FixedPoint/QFloat representation. Standard integer QAT, not threshold-balancing/rate-coding calibration; there is no weight-normalization pass calibrated to a target firing rate over a chosen T, and no iterative rate-coding simulation.

quartz.name: Quartz
quartz.summary: Lenz, Orchard, Sheik's time-to-first-spike (TTFS) ANN-to-SNN converter for Loihi, explicitly not rate-coded; states plainly that prior temporal-coding conversion methods had not been demonstrated on physical neuromorphic hardware before this work, and that "no soft reset of membrane potentials [is] needed" because TTFS neurons fire at most once.

rank-order-coding.name: Rank order coding (ROC)
rank-order-coding.summary: Information is carried entirely by the relative order in which a population's neurons fire (each firing at most once), not by rate or absolute timing; contrast-invariant and decoded via feedforward shunting inhibition. No published ANN-to-SNN conversion method targets ROC, because the rate/count-matching correspondence theorems underlying QCFS-style conversion are cardinal (magnitude-matching) while ROC's content is purely ordinal (a permutation).

rate-coding.name: Rate / count coding
rate-coding.summary: The number of spikes over T timesteps represents a scalar value; under reset-by-subtraction and a fixed threshold, achievable spike counts {0,...,T} form an inherently uniform T-level quantizer, directly linking rate coding to uniform quantization-aware training.

reset-by-subtraction.name: Reset by subtraction (soft reset)
reset-by-subtraction.summary: V(t) = V(t-1) + z(t) - V_thr, carrying excess charge above threshold forward into the next integration window; proven by Rueckauer et al. to make the SNN's time-averaged firing rate converge exactly to the target ANN activation as T -> infinity, with error only from discrete sampling, not a persistent bias. Required by essentially all rate-coded ANN-to-SNN conversion theory (Diehl 2015, Rueckauer 2017, QCFS-family work).

reset-to-zero.name: Reset to zero (hard reset)
reset-to-zero.summary: V(t) forced to a fixed baseline (typically 0) whenever the neuron fires, discarding the residual charge epsilon = n*z - V_thr above threshold at every reset event; this residual is a systematic, input-dependent bias that compounds across layers and does not vanish with longer simulation time. Rueckauer et al.'s own CIFAR-10 ablation: switching only the reset mechanism (holding Poisson input and normalization fixed) improved accuracy by roughly 20 percentage points.

riscv-accelerator.name: RISC-V SNN Accelerator
riscv-accelerator.summary: A RISC-V-based soft vector processor tailored to simulating SNNs, realized as a soft core on an AMD/Xilinx Kria KV260 FPGA board. The survey's evidence records measure FeNN's single-core recurrent spoken-digit classifier against an embedded GPU and Loihi, and FeNN-DMA's balanced-random-network simulation throughput, classification accuracy, and post-implementation operating frequency and power on the same board family.

robotics-closed-loop-control.name: Robotics and closed-loop control
robotics-closed-loop-control.summary: The second-largest genuinely end-to-end (sensing-to-actuation) spiking-hardware application category after gesture recognition, spanning hand-designed motor-control circuits, gradient-trained spiking policies, and one hardware-adaptation (rescaling) step layered on top of gradient training.

rockpool.name: Rockpool
rockpool.summary: SynSense's second SNN library, targeting deployment to the Xylo family; mapper()/quantize_methods()/config_from_specification() pipeline deploys to XyloSamna/XyloMonitor on physical hardware or the bit-precise XyloSim simulator.

samna.name: samna
samna.summary: SynSense's cross-chip developer interface and runtime environment ("the developer interface to the SynSense toolchain and run-time environment for interacting with all SynSense devices"): a Python API with a C++ core, applying device configuration objects (apply_configuration(cfg)) and streaming real-time event data through an EventFilterGraph of source/sink nodes and JIT-compiled filters.

sigma-delta.name: Sigma-delta / graded / delta modulation
sigma-delta.summary: Wraps a conventional activation with a delta encoder (transmits only the change since last transmitted value, above a threshold) and a sigma (running-sum) decoder, exploiting temporal redundancy in addition to spatial sparsity. Enabled at hardware level on Loihi 2 by native graded spikes carrying up to 24-bit signed integer magnitude.

signed-spikes.name: Signed spikes
signed-spikes.summary: A spike event whose payload or channel encodes sign, used to represent a negative delta or gradient rather than only a positive one. Native only on Loihi 2, via its signed graded-spike payload; every other reviewed platform fakes a signed quantity with two unsigned channels, doubling wiring or neuron cost.

silicon-cochlea.name: Silicon cochlea
silicon-cochlea.summary: An event-based analog/mixed-signal audio front end that converts sound directly into a spike train (rather than a sampled PCM waveform), used as the sensing front end behind spike-domain audio benchmarks such as the Spiking Heidelberg Digits (SHD) and Spiking Speech Commands (SSC) datasets.

sinabs.name: Sinabs
sinabs.summary: SynSense's PyTorch-based SNN library with a first-party deployment path to Speck/DYNAP-CNN; from_model() defaults to MembraneSubtract() (reset-by-subtraction), matching the Speck hardware default; no dedicated BatchNorm-fold utility documented (users must fold/avoid BN before conversion).

single-pass.name: Single pass, T collapsed
single-pass.summary: Execution collapses to one hardware pass over quantized, integer-only activations rather than a multi-timestep rate-coded simulation loop: a 'spike'/'event' is a nonzero (or newly-changed) quantized activation value, with no membrane potential accumulating over a user-specified T. The standard converted-CNN execution model on BrainChip Akida.

slam.name: SLAM and localization
slam.summary: SLAM/VIO is almost entirely a GPU/embedded-CPU/FPGA workload in the recent event-camera literature, with a single narrow hand-designed exception (unidimensional head-direction SLAM) reaching physical Loihi.

snn-toolbox.name: SNN Toolbox
snn-toolbox.summary: Rueckauer et al.'s reference implementation of percentile-based weight/threshold-normalization ANN-to-SNN conversion with reset-by-subtraction IF neurons (Rueckauer 2017), the direct ancestor of the NxTF/Loihi pipeline; dormant since ~2021-2022 (last substantive release March 2021, last patches August 2022).

snntorch.name: snnTorch
snntorch.summary: PyTorch-native SNN training library (Eshraghian et al., Proc. IEEE 2023); snn.Leaky defaults to reset_mechanism='subtract' (soft reset); no official first-party deployment path to physical silicon was located, though third-party NIR export exists.

speck.name: SynSense Speck
speck.summary: Fully asynchronous, clockless SoC integrating a 128x128 on-chip Dynamic Vision Sensor with the DYNAP-CNN convolutional neuromorphic processor (9 fixed conv->IF->pool cores, up to ~328K neurons). Measured sub-4-microsecond end-to-end 9-layer propagation latency, with reset-by-subtraction as the documented hardware default.

spike-time-gradient-methods.name: Spike-time gradient methods (SLAYER / EXODUS / EventProp)
spike-time-gradient-methods.summary: Gradient methods that assign error through spike timing rather than plain surrogate-derivative BPTT on a fixed grid. Within this lineage SLAYER is itself a surrogate-gradient method (a stochastic spike-escape-rate derivative shapes its backward pass), while EventProp is the exact one, differentiating analytically through the spike event. The one direct-training lineage with a consistently exercised, vendor-maintained silicon path, SLAYER/Lava-DL to Loihi, and EventProp/mlGeNN to Loihi 2.

spikingjelly.name: SpikingJelly
spikingjelly.summary: PyTorch-based, full-stack SNN toolkit (Science Advances 2023) with CuPy/Triton-accelerated training, an ann2snn conversion module (rewritten into an FX-graph recipe framework, current flagship recipe no longer cites Rueckauer/Diehl), and export paths to Lava (lava_exchange), NIR (nir_exchange), and Lynxi. Actively maintained.

spinnaker-1.name: SpiNNaker 1
spinnaker-1.summary: Manycore ARM968-based digital neuromorphic manycore system (18 cores/chip, GALS architecture, up to ~1.04M cores at full 10-cabinet scale) that simulates arbitrary software-defined neuron models at a default 1 ms real-time timestep, communicating via best-effort (drop-possible) AER packets over a custom asynchronous router fabric.

spinnaker-2.name: SpiNNaker 2
spinnaker-2.summary: Successor chip (22 nm FDSOI, ARM Cortex-M4F cores with FPU, 144 PEs/chip) adding a 16x4 INT8 MAC accelerator per processing element for hybrid dense-ANN/spiking execution; commercialized by SpiNNcloud Systems and deployed at multi-billion-neuron scale (Dresden, Sandia, Leipzig).

spinnaker-runtime.name: SpiNNaker runtime
spinnaker-runtime.summary: The on-chip SpiN1API event-driven operating system plus the host-side SpiNNTools data-loading/execution/extraction pipeline that actually runs a placed-and-routed machine graph on physical SpiNNaker silicon: per-core neuron/synapse parameter blocks and synaptic-matrix data are generated on the host and loaded into each core's ITCM/DTCM/SDRAM, all cores are signaled to start together, SpiN1API then runs the compiled C executable on each core for the configured duration, and results are read back off-machine via the PyNN API. For SpiNNaker 2, the analogous py-spinnaker2 'experiment runner' partitions and executes single-chip or 48-chip systems, with a Brian2-based software-emulation fallback when no chip is available.

spynnaker.name: sPyNNaker
spynnaker.summary: The PyNN backend (pyNN.spiNNaker) plus SpiNNTools execution engine that translates a PyNN network into an application graph, partitions it into a machine graph (~256 atoms/core given per-core SDRAM/DTCM budgets), places/routes it onto SpiNNaker cores (compressing routing tables to the ~1024-entry-per-chip router budget), loads compiled C executables, and extracts results after execution.

static-frames.name: Static frames
static-frames.summary: Conventional dense RGB/grayscale image input (MNIST/CIFAR/ImageNet-scale datasets), the default representation of both the classical/QCFS-lineage ANN-to-SNN conversion literature and any converted-CNN deployment (Akida, Loihi via SNN Toolbox/NxTF).

sync-tick.name: Synchronous global tick
sync-tick.summary: Every core advances the same discrete time index in lockstep, enforced by an explicit barrier handshake (Loihi), a hardware timer interrupt (SpiNNaker), or a single global clock signal (TrueNorth, Tianjic). T is a logical/synchronization unit whose wall-clock duration is not fixed by the timestep count alone.

syncnn.name: SyncNN
syncnn.summary: FPGA-based (Xilinx ZCU102/ZCU104/ZED, physical boards) rate-encoding IF accelerator that mathematically proves a synchronous reformulation of standard multi-timestep asynchronous IF+reset-by-subtraction execution: only the Poisson input-encoding layer runs for the full T-step window, downstream layers compute the equivalent spike count in one shot via Vm/Vth division.

tactile-sensor.name: Tactile sensor
tactile-sensor.summary: A touch/e-skin sensor whose output is converted into DVS-like or spike-domain events before reaching a spiking chip: a GelSight optical-tactile front end generating marker-motion events (GelNeuro), or a fiber-Bragg-grating (FBG) e-skin generating touch events (DYNAP-SE tactile localization).

tianjic.name: Tsinghua Tianjic
tianjic.summary: Many-core, reconfigurable hybrid chip explicitly designed to run both ANNs and SNNs on the same silicon using a shared axon/synapse/dendrite/soma/router abstraction; demonstrated driving an unmanned bicycle performing simultaneous real-time perception and control tasks. Commercial lineage continues via Lynxi's KA200/HP300 products.

time-series.name: Sampled time series
time-series.summary: Sampled sequential/time-domain sensor data (audio, surface EMG, scalp EEG, IMU, force-torque, encoder feedback) consumed by directly trained or hardware-in-the-loop-trained SNNs, rather than a static-image ANN converted to spikes.

tracking-motion.name: Tracking and motion estimation
tracking-motion.summary: Optical flow, feature tracking, and motion estimation from vision (usually event-camera) input. Overwhelmingly a GPU/workstation and embedded-CPU/Jetson workload in the surveyed literature; essentially absent from genuine neuromorphic silicon, in contrast to gesture recognition and simple closed-loop robot control.

truenorth.name: IBM TrueNorth
truenorth.summary: Fully digital, event-driven neurosynaptic chip (28 nm, 4096 cores, 1M neurons, 256M synapses, ~65-70 mW) evaluated once per 1 kHz global "tick"; its Eedn training/deployment methodology encodes activation magnitude spatially across redundant trinary-weighted neuron copies within a single tick, not via multi-timestep temporal rate accumulation. Discontinued; superseded conceptually by the non-spiking NorthPole NPU.

ttfs.name: Time-to-first-spike (TTFS) / latency coding
ttfs.summary: Each neuron fires at most once; the timing of that single spike encodes the value. Achieves extreme sparsity but requires long training-time windows for useful spike-time gradients, and firing times must be quantized on real hardware (reintroducing a quantization floor). No soft reset of membrane potentials is needed for TTFS coding since neurons fire at most once.

ttfs-cnn-to-snn-conversion.name: TTFS CNN-to-SNN Conversion Pipeline
ttfs-cnn-to-snn-conversion.summary: A custom CNN-to-SNN, time-to-first-spike (TTFS) conversion pipeline, described in an analog-mixed-signal-chip paper as the digital-baseline path against an Innatera SNP analog comparator. The retrieved text does not name this pipeline after any public library; it is not SNN Toolbox and does not state a CMSIS-NN kernel stage.

ttfs-mcu-firmware.name: TTFS-Converted-Network MCU Deployment
ttfs-mcu-firmware.summary: The deployed form of a CNN-to-SNN, time-to-first-spike-converted digital network on the ARM Cortex-M4 MCU. The paper says only that the converted SNN is deployed on the MCU and describes the digital SNN as either software-simulated or hardware-accelerated; it never uses the words firmware or compiled. CMSIS-NN is named in the paper only as a comparator framework and SNN Toolbox is not mentioned, so this node is named from the paper's own description, 'custom CNN-to-SNN (TTFS) conversion pipeline,' rather than from either named library.

xylo.name: SynSense Xylo
xylo.summary: Separate SynSense digital SNN inference ASIC family for audio/IMU/low-dimensional sensory signals (XyloAudio 2/3, XyloIMU), genuinely clocked and synchronous (up to 50-100 MHz internal clock, global timestep dt), with native subtractive reset and up to 31 output spikes per neuron per timestep.

xylo-mapper.name: Rockpool Xylo mapper/quantizer
xylo-mapper.summary: Rockpool's mapper() extracts a hardware specification from a trained computational graph and DRC-checks it against Xylo's CuBa-LIF architecture constraints; quantize_methods (global_quantize / channel_quantize) quantizes weights/thresholds to 8-bit weights and 16-bit thresholds by default; config_from_specification() builds the final hardware configuration object.

xylo-sim.name: Xylo simulator (XyloSim)
xylo-sim.summary: Rockpool's bit-precise XyloSim simulator of the Xylo digital SNN core, run on the host CPU. It steps the same synchronous, time-stepped spiking LIF neurons with exponential input synapses that the Xylo hardware implements, so a network can be trained and checked before deployment. A run here claims a simulation of the Xylo core, not a measurement on Xylo silicon.
